title: The directed set of finite subextensions of an algebraic closure
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $\mathbf Q_\ell$ the field of $\ell$-adic numbers [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ a fixed algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $\mathcal E_\ell$ be the set of intermediate fields $\mathbf Q_\ell\subset E\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ that are finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], that is, finite-dimensional as $\mathbf Q_\ell$-vector spaces, ordered by inclusion. For $E,E'\in\mathcal E_\ell$ the *compositum* $EE'\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ is the smallest subfield of $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ containing $E$ and $E'$; it is again finite over $\mathbf Q_\ell$ (it is the image of $E\otimes_{\mathbf Q_\ell}E'$, of dimension at most $[E:\mathbf Q_\ell]\,[E':\mathbf Q_\ell]$). Hence $\mathcal E_\ell$ is nonempty (it contains $\mathbf Q_\ell$) and *directed*: any two elements $E,E'$ have a common upper bound $L\supset E,E'$ in $\mathcal E_\ell$, namely $EE'$. Every element of $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ lies in some $E\in\mathcal E_\ell$ (namely $\mathbf Q_\ell(\alpha)$, finite since $\alpha$ is algebraic), so $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell=\bigcup_{E\in\mathcal E_\ell}E$. For $E\subset L$ in $\mathcal E_\ell$, $L$ is a finite extension of $E$.
